guides.title: How to get what you need

wordpress.s1: Sign in to your WordPress admin (usually yoursite.com/wp-admin).
wordpress.s3: Scroll to Application Passwords, type a name such as Rankoya and click Add New Application Password.
wordpress.s4: Copy the password WordPress shows, spaces and all. It's only shown once.
wordpress.s5: Paste it here, with your site's address and the username you sign in with.
wordpress.note: Your user needs to be an Editor or Administrator. Application Passwords need WordPress 5.6 or later and a site on https; some security plugins switch them off.

wordpressCom.s2: Sign in with the account that manages your blog, then click Approve.
wordpressCom.s3: Back in Rankoya, choose which of your WordPress.com sites to publish to.
wordpressCom.note: You need to be an administrator of that WordPress.com site.

shopify.s1: Open the <link>Shopify Dev Dashboard</link> and create an app for your store.
shopify.s2: In the app's settings, add the scopes read_content and write_content, then release a version.
shopify.s3: Install the app on your store from the app's overview page.
shopify.s4: In the app's Settings, copy the Client ID and Client secret.
shopify.s5: Paste them below with your store's address ending in .myshopify.com, then click Get access token and Connect.
shopify.note: Shopify's tokens for these apps last 24 hours. If publishing stops working, get a new token and reconnect.

webflow.s1: Open your site in the Webflow dashboard and go to Site settings › Apps & integrations.
webflow.s2: Under API access, click Generate API token, name it Rankoya and allow CMS: read and write and Sites: read.
webflow.s3: Copy the token. It's only shown once.
webflow.s4: In the Designer, open CMS, then your blog collection's settings, and copy the Collection ID.
webflow.s5: Paste the token and the Collection ID here.
webflow.note: The collection needs fields for the post's title, slug and body. Ask your developer if you're not sure which collection is your blog.

wix.s1: Open the Wix API Keys page and click Generate API Key.
wix.s2: Name it Rankoya, pick your site and allow the Blog permissions, then generate it.
wix.s3: Copy the key. It's only shown once.
wix.s4: Open your site's dashboard: the site ID is the code in the address bar right after /dashboard/.
wix.s5: Paste the key and the site ID here.
wix.note: You need to be the site owner, or have API key permissions on the Wix account.

ghost.s1: In Ghost Admin, go to Settings › Integrations.
ghost.s2: Click Add custom integration and name it Rankoya.
ghost.s3: Copy the Admin API key (it looks like id:secret) and the API URL.
ghost.s4: Paste the API URL as your Ghost site address, and the Admin API key here.
ghost.note: Custom integrations are available on every Ghost plan, including Ghost(Pro) Starter.

searchConsole.s1: Make sure your site is added in Google Search Console. A Domain property is best.
searchConsole.s2: Click Continue with Google and sign in with the Google account that owns the site there.
searchConsole.s3: Allow Rankoya to view your Search Console data. It's read-only; Rankoya can't change anything.
searchConsole.s4: Back in Rankoya, pick your site's property. Your Google data starts syncing straight away.
searchConsole.note: New properties can take a few days to show data in Search Console.

nextjs.s1: Choose Connect. There's nothing to fill in.
nextjs.s2: When an article is ready, open it in Rankoya and click Publish. Rankoya prepares it to copy.
nextjs.s3: Copy the HTML (or the text) and add it to your app, for example as a new page, an MDX file or an entry in your CMS.
nextjs.s4: Use the title, meta description and URL slug Rankoya gives you, then deploy.
nextjs.note: Want articles to go live by themselves? Your developer can add a publishing endpoint later; ask us about webhooks.

manual.s1: Choose Connect. There's nothing to fill in.
manual.s2: When an article is ready, open it in Rankoya and click Publish. Rankoya prepares it to copy.
manual.s3: Copy it into your site's editor, with the title, meta description and URL slug Rankoya gives you, and publish it there.
manual.note: Works with any site, including Lovable, Replit and site builders Rankoya doesn't connect to yet.

meta.title: Page title and description check
meta.body: Shows the title, description and headings Google reads on a page, and flags anything missing or too long.
meta.failed: Couldn't read that page. Check the URL, then try again.
meta.why: The title and description are what people see in Google before they click. Clear ones get more clicks.
meta.when: You've published a page, changed its wording, or a page gets seen but rarely clicked.

redirects.title: Redirect check
redirects.body: Follows a link step by step and shows every place it sends visitors, and how long each step takes.
redirects.failed: Couldn't check that URL. Try again.
redirects.summary: {count, plural, one {# redirect to {url}} other {# redirects to {url}}}
redirects.noRedirect: No redirect. The URL answers with status {status}.
redirects.why: Long chains of redirects slow pages down and can lose the ranking a page has earned.
redirects.when: You've moved a page, changed your domain, or a link lands somewhere unexpected.

broken.title: Broken link check
broken.body: Checks up to 100 links on a page and lists the ones that lead nowhere.
broken.failed: Couldn't check that page. Try again.
broken.why: Links that lead to error pages frustrate visitors and tell Google the page isn't looked after.
broken.when: Before a page goes live, and every few months on your most visited pages.

robots.title: Robots.txt check
robots.body: Shows the rules your site gives search engines and AI crawlers about which pages they may read, and where your sitemap is.
robots.why: One wrong rule here can hide your whole site from Google or from AI assistants.
robots.when: Your pages aren't showing up in Google, or you've just launched or rebuilt the site.

clustering.title: Group keywords into topics
clustering.body: Paste a list of searches and Rankoya groups the ones that mean the same thing, so each group can become one page.
clustering.placeholder: One per line, or separated by commas
clustering.failed: Couldn't cluster these keywords. Try again.
clustering.why: One strong page per topic ranks better than several thin pages competing with each other.
clustering.when: You have a long list of keyword ideas and want to plan which pages to write.
